manifest.title: A Verified Lean Core for Lax Validation

inputs.abstract:
# A verified Lean core for Lax validation

Lax records proofs that may depend on statements not yet proved. To determine
which statements are established, it must follow these dependencies without
treating circular reasoning as a proof. We implement a validation core in Lean
and prove its main guarantees.

The core finds every axiom used by a declaration, checks the mathematical
validation rules, and computes exactly the statements that follow from the
available proofs and declared assumptions. We also verify a certificate checker:
an accepted certificate accounts for every derivable statement, and every
well-formed network has such a certificate with at most one step per statement.
A controller requires matching reports of successful replay and inspection for
the same identified artifact, and any failed stage prevents approval.

The main theorem shows that every unconditional proved label returned by the
combined entry point is sound under an explicit contract for Lean's kernel and
faithful inspection. All 26 theorem statements have kernel-replayed proofs,
with their dependencies recorded in the proof network. These guarantees concern
the executable Lean functions defined here. Using them in the live Lax service
still requires integration with source acquisition, input extraction, authentic
runner reports, execution, and publication.

concepts.title: Certificates for the exact set of established statements
concepts.description:
A certificate is a list of statements paired with their chosen proofs, in
dependency order. Each proof must use only initial assumptions or statements
already established earlier in the list. A final check requires the resulting
set to be closed under every rule in the network.

The ordered witnesses show that nothing was falsely added. The closure check
shows that nothing derivable was omitted. Thus one certificate can justify
both the proved and unproved classifications for an entire snapshot.
Unproved here means not derivable from the available rules; it does not mean
that the mathematical statement is false.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.ProofNetworks

/-!
---
title: Certificates for the exact set of established statements
type: theorem
---
A certificate is a list of statements paired with their chosen proofs, in
dependency order. Each proof must use only initial assumptions or statements
already established earlier in the list. A final check requires the resulting
set to be closed under every rule in the network.

The ordered witnesses show that nothing was falsely added. The closure check
shows that nothing derivable was omitted. Thus one certificate can justify
both the proved and unproved classifications for an entire snapshot.
Unproved here means not derivable from the available rules; it does not mean
that the mathematical statement is false.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Certificates

open Declarations ProofNetworks

/-- A step names the statement being established and the proof rule used. -/
structure Step where
  statement : Nat
  proofId : Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Check witnesses in order; each new statement must have a grounded proof. -/
def checkSteps (n : Network) : List Nat → List Step → Option (List Nat)
  | known, [] => some known.eraseDups
  | known, step :: rest =>
      if !known.contains step.statement && n.rules.any (fun r =>
          r.proofId == step.proofId && r.conclusion == step.statement &&
          includes known r.assumptions) then
        checkSteps n (known ++ [step.statement]) rest
      else none

/-- Check that every enabled proof rule has its conclusion in the result. -/
def checkClosed (n : Network) (known : List Nat) : Bool :=
  n.rules.all (fun r => !(includes known r.assumptions) || known.contains r.conclusion)

/-- Proposed production entry point for checking an entire classification. -/
def check (n : Network) (initial : List Nat) (steps : List Step) : Option (List Nat) :=
  match checkSteps n initial steps with
  | none => none
  | some known => if checkClosed n known then some known else none

/-- An accepted certificate describes precisely all derivable statements. -/
axiom check_exact (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) (steps : List Step)
    (known : List Nat) (accepted : check n initial steps = some known) (a : Nat) :
    a ∈ known ↔ Derivable n initial a

/-- Every well-formed finite network has a certificate of at most one step
per statement. The producer is not assumed to be correct or trusted. -/
axiom certificate_exists (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) :
    ∃ steps known, steps.length ≤ n.statements.length ∧
      check n initial steps = some known

/-- A statement excluded by an accepted certificate has no finite derivation
in this network from these initial assumptions. -/
axiom unproved_certificate (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) (steps : List Step)
    (known : List Nat) (accepted : check n initial steps = some known)
    (a : Nat) (excluded : a ∉ known) : ¬ Derivable n initial a

end Lax796640.Certificates

  Lax796640.ProofNetworks.WellFormed n →
    ∀ (initial : List Nat),
      (∀ (a : Nat), List.instMembership.mem initial a → List.instMembership.mem n.statements a) →
        Exists fun steps =>
          Exists fun known =>
            And (instLENat.le steps.length n.statements.length)
              (Eq (Lax796640.Certificates.check n initial steps) (Option.some known))

        ∀ (steps : List Lax796640.Certificates.Step) (known : List Nat),
          Eq (Lax796640.Certificates.check n initial steps) (Option.some known) →

concepts.title: The finite input to the validator
concepts.description:
The validator receives a finite table of packages and Lean declarations.
A declaration is a named constant, such as a definition, an axiom, or a
theorem. Its references include constants used in both its type and its body,
and structural links such as an inductive declaration's constructors.

Natural numbers are internal identifiers. Names are retained for readers and
for identifying the three permitted background axioms. Distinct declarations
must have distinct identifiers and names; the validation rules check this.

This is the proposed interface of a production Lean component. An adapter
must obtain these facts from the same artifacts that passed kernel replay.
An input record containing `true` does not itself establish that fact.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic

/-!
---
title: The finite input to the validator
type: definition
---
The validator receives a finite table of packages and Lean declarations.
A declaration is a named constant, such as a definition, an axiom, or a
theorem. Its references include constants used in both its type and its body,
and structural links such as an inductive declaration's constructors.

Natural numbers are internal identifiers. Names are retained for readers and
for identifying the three permitted background axioms. Distinct declarations
must have distinct identifiers and names; the validation rules check this.

This is the proposed interface of a production Lean component. An adapter
must obtain these facts from the same artifacts that passed kernel replay.
An input record containing `true` does not itself establish that fact.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Declarations

/-- Background packages are the pinned Lean and Mathlib environment. -/
inductive PackageRole where
  | background
  | concepts
  | proofs
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Only the distinctions needed for the mathematical validation rules. -/
inductive DeclarationKind where
  | axiomDecl
  | theoremDecl
  | other
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- A package and the packages it directly requires. -/
structure Package where
  id : Nat
  role : PackageRole
  environment : String
  registered : Bool
  requires : List Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Facts extracted from one kernel-checked declaration. -/
structure Declaration where
  id : Nat
  name : String
  package : Nat
  kind : DeclarationKind
  /-- Whether the declared type itself has type `Prop`. -/
  isProposition : Bool
  /-- References from types, bodies, and structural links to constructors. -/
  references : List Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- A kernel comparison and an import check for a proposed conclusion. -/
structure Comparison where
  theoremId : Nat
  statementId : Nat
  sameType : Bool
  conclusionImported : Bool
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- An author's request to record a theorem as a proof of a statement. -/
structure Claim where
  theoremId : Nat
  statementId : Nat
  /-- Optional documentation, cross-checked against computed dependencies. -/
  claimedAssumptions : Option (List Nat)
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- One environment and its complete relevant declaration table.
`localPackages` are being validated now; other non-background packages must
already be registered. Imported packages still have their declarations here.
-/
structure Snapshot where
  environment : String
  localPackages : List Nat
  packages : List Package
  declarations : List Declaration
  comparisons : List Comparison
  claims : List Claim
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Find a declaration. Duplicate identifiers are rejected before acceptance. -/
def declaration (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : Option Declaration :=
  s.declarations.find? (fun d => d.id == id)

/-- Find a package by its identifier. -/
def package (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : Option Package :=
  s.packages.find? (fun p => p.id == id)

/-- Every requested identifier belongs to the supplied list. -/
def includes (available requested : List Nat) : Bool :=
  requested.all available.contains

/-- Set equality ignores order and repeated identifiers. -/
def sameMembers (left right : List Nat) : Bool :=
  includes left right && includes right left

/-- The graph conditions needed for bounded dependency traversal. -/
def ReferencesWellFormed (s : Snapshot) : Prop :=
  (s.declarations.map Declaration.id).Nodup ∧
  ∀ d ∈ s.declarations, ∀ id ∈ d.references,
    ∃ target ∈ s.declarations, target.id = id

end Lax796640.Declarations

concepts.title: Finding every axiom used by a declaration
concepts.description:
A declaration depends on an axiom when following constant references can
reach that axiom. We include a path of length zero: an axiom uses itself.
References in types matter as well as references in proof bodies.

The executable collector expands the set of reachable declarations once per
round. There are at most as many necessary rounds as declarations. This
handles cycles without relying on recursive calls through the graph.

The two statements below are proof obligations. They concern the concrete
functions in this file, given a complete finite reference table. Establishing
that an inspector supplies that table is a separate integration obligation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.Declarations

/-!
---
title: Finding every axiom used by a declaration
type: theorem
---
A declaration depends on an axiom when following constant references can
reach that axiom. We include a path of length zero: an axiom uses itself.
References in types matter as well as references in proof bodies.

The executable collector expands the set of reachable declarations once per
round. There are at most as many necessary rounds as declarations. This
handles cycles without relying on recursive calls through the graph.

The two statements below are proof obligations. They concern the concrete
functions in this file, given a complete finite reference table. Establishing
that an inspector supplies that table is a separate integration obligation.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Dependencies

open Declarations

/-- The direct references of a declaration; absent entries have no references.
Missing referenced declarations are nevertheless rejected by validation. -/
def references (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((declaration s id).map Declaration.references).getD []

/-- A finite path in the graph of constant references. -/
inductive Reaches (s : Snapshot) : Nat → Nat → Prop where
  | self (id : Nat) : Reaches s id id
  | next {start middle finish : Nat} :
      Reaches s start middle → finish ∈ references s middle →
      Reaches s start finish

/-- One round retains known declarations and adds their direct references. -/
def expand (s : Snapshot) (known : List Nat) : List Nat :=
  (known ++ known.flatMap (references s)).eraseDups

/-- Run a fixed number of rounds, using ordinary recursion on a natural number. -/
def expandFor (s : Snapshot) : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | 0, known => known
  | rounds + 1, known => expandFor s rounds (expand s known)

/-- The proposed executable collector, with its finite bound built in. -/
def reachable (s : Snapshot) (start : Nat) : List Nat :=
  expandFor s s.declarations.length [start]

/-- Test the recorded kind of a declaration. -/
def isAxiom (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : Bool :=
  (declaration s id).any (fun d => d.kind == .axiomDecl)

/-- The specification of an axiom dependency uses finite paths. -/
def UsesAxiom (s : Snapshot) (start axiomId : Nat) : Prop :=
  Reaches s start axiomId ∧ isAxiom s axiomId = true

/-- Compute dependencies from references, never from an author's claimed list. -/
def axiomsUsed (s : Snapshot) (start : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (reachable s start).filter (isAxiom s)

/-- The bounded traversal finds exactly the reachable declarations. -/
axiom reachable_exact (s : Snapshot) (h : ReferencesWellFormed s)
    (start : Nat) (existsStart : ∃ d ∈ s.declarations, d.id = start) (id : Nat) :
    id ∈ reachable s start ↔ Reaches s start id

/-- No used axiom is omitted, and no unrelated axiom is reported. -/
axiom axiomsUsed_exact (s : Snapshot) (h : ReferencesWellFormed s)
    (start : Nat) (existsStart : ∃ d ∈ s.declarations, d.id = start) (id : Nat) :
    id ∈ axiomsUsed s start ↔ UsesAxiom s start id

end Lax796640.Dependencies

statements.signature:
axiomsUsed_exact : ∀ (s : Lax796640.Declarations.Snapshot),
  Lax796640.Declarations.ReferencesWellFormed s →
    ∀ (start : Nat),
      (Exists fun d => And (List.instMembership.mem s.declarations d) (Eq d.id start)) →
        ∀ (id : Nat),
          Iff (List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.Dependencies.axiomsUsed s start) id)
            (Lax796640.Dependencies.UsesAxiom s start id)
statements.doc: No used axiom is omitted, and no unrelated axiom is reported.

statements.signature:
reachable_exact : ∀ (s : Lax796640.Declarations.Snapshot),
  Lax796640.Declarations.ReferencesWellFormed s →
    ∀ (start : Nat),
      (Exists fun d => And (List.instMembership.mem s.declarations d) (Eq d.id start)) →
        ∀ (id : Nat),
          Iff (List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.Dependencies.reachable s start) id)
            (Lax796640.Dependencies.Reaches s start id)
statements.doc: The bounded traversal finds exactly the reachable declarations.

concepts.title: Requiring the right checks before approval
concepts.description:
The proposed controller records successful concept replay, successful proof
replay, and inspection for one identified artifact. Receipts for another
artifact are ignored. Any failure blocks approval for the rest of this run.
A new artifact begins a new run with no inherited receipts.

Artifact identifiers include the source commit, environment, captured files,
and dependency snapshot. Equality of these strings is the controller's check;
computing authentic digests and keeping the represented files immutable are
obligations of the external runner. Similarly, a replay event is a receipt
from the runner, not a formal proof of kernel execution.

The functions here are intended to be used by the production controller.
The stated guarantees are about these exact functions. Their adoption by the
current Node pipeline is still planned work.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.Validation

/-!
---
title: Requiring the right checks before approval
type: theorem
---
The proposed controller records successful concept replay, successful proof
replay, and inspection for one identified artifact. Receipts for another
artifact are ignored. Any failure blocks approval for the rest of this run.
A new artifact begins a new run with no inherited receipts.

Artifact identifiers include the source commit, environment, captured files,
and dependency snapshot. Equality of these strings is the controller's check;
computing authentic digests and keeping the represented files immutable are
obligations of the external runner. Similarly, a replay event is a receipt
from the runner, not a formal proof of kernel execution.

The functions here are intended to be used by the production controller.
The stated guarantees are about these exact functions. Their adoption by the
current Node pipeline is still planned work.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Pipeline

open Declarations Validation

/-- The identity shared by replay, inspection, and the eventual publication. -/
structure ArtifactKey where
  sourceCommit : String
  environment : String
  captureDigest : String
  dependencyDigest : String
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Reports from the external runner. Authenticating them is outside this controller. -/
inductive Event where
  | conceptsReplayed (key : ArtifactKey)
  | proofsReplayed (key : ArtifactKey)
  | inspected (key : ArtifactKey) (data : Snapshot)
  | failed
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Accumulated evidence for one artifact. -/
structure State where
  key : ArtifactKey
  conceptsReplayed : Bool
  proofsReplayed : Bool
  inspection : Option Snapshot
  failed : Bool
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Starting a run clears every receipt, even if another run just succeeded. -/
def start (key : ArtifactKey) : State :=
  { key, conceptsReplayed := false, proofsReplayed := false,
    inspection := none, failed := false }

/-- Advance the controller. A failure is permanent within this run. -/
def step (state : State) (event : Event) : State :=
  if state.failed then state else
  match event with
  | .failed => { state with failed := true }
  | .conceptsReplayed key =>
      if key == state.key then { state with conceptsReplayed := true } else state
  | .proofsReplayed key =>
      if key == state.key then { state with proofsReplayed := true } else state
  | .inspected key data =>
      if key == state.key then { state with inspection := some data } else state

/-- Execute a finite sequence of runner events. -/
def run (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event) : State :=
  events.foldl step (start key)

/-- Approval requires both replays, an inspection in this environment,
and acceptance by the concrete mathematical validator. -/
def approve (state : State) : Bool :=
  !state.failed && state.conceptsReplayed && state.proofsReplayed &&
    state.inspection.any (fun data =>
      data.environment == state.key.environment && validate data)

/-- The exact inspected input approved at the end of this run, if any. -/
def approvedInput (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event) : Option Snapshot :=
  let state := run key events
  if approve state then state.inspection else none

/-- A declarative record of the required successful stages. -/
def EvidenceComplete (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event) (data : Snapshot) : Prop :=
  Event.conceptsReplayed key ∈ events ∧ Event.proofsReplayed key ∈ events ∧
  Event.inspected key data ∈ events ∧ Event.failed ∉ events ∧
  data.environment = key.environment ∧ Valid data

/-- An approved input has all required evidence for the same artifact. -/
axiom approval_requires_evidence (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (data : Snapshot) (accepted : approvedInput key events = some data) :
    EvidenceComplete key events data

/-- A failed stage can never be repaired merely by later success receipts. -/
axiom failure_blocks_approval (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (failed : Event.failed ∈ events) : approvedInput key events = none

/-- Starting a new run carries no approval from a previous artifact. -/
axiom fresh_run_unapproved (key : ArtifactKey) : approve (start key) = false

end Lax796640.Pipeline

  (data : Lax796640.Declarations.Snapshot),
  Eq (Lax796640.Pipeline.approvedInput key events) (Option.some data) →
    Lax796640.Pipeline.EvidenceComplete key events data
statements.doc: An approved input has all required evidence for the same artifact.

statements.signature:

  List.instMembership.mem events Lax796640.Pipeline.Event.failed →
    Eq (Lax796640.Pipeline.approvedInput key events) Option.none
statements.doc: A failed stage can never be repaired merely by later success receipts.

statements.doc: Starting a new run carries no approval from a previous artifact.

concepts.title: The proposed production entry points and their guarantees
concepts.description:
The functions in this file combine the controller, validation rules, and
certificate checker. The implementation to deploy is these same Lean
definitions, not a separately handwritten translation of them.

The general entry point reports the assumptions under which its results hold.
The entry point for ordinary proved labels always supplies an empty assumption
list. This prevents a conditional classification from silently being
presented as an unconditional proof.

The theorem statements are proved in the separate proof package. Replaying
that package checks their proofs. Deployment still requires faithful input
extraction, authentic runner receipts, correct execution, and a publisher that
respects rejection and publishes the very artifact identified by the approved
run.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.Pipeline
import Lax796640.RelativeSoundness

/-!
---
title: The proposed production entry points and their guarantees
type: theorem
---
The functions in this file combine the controller, validation rules, and
certificate checker. The implementation to deploy is these same Lean
definitions, not a separately handwritten translation of them.

The general entry point reports the assumptions under which its results hold.
The entry point for ordinary proved labels always supplies an empty assumption
list. This prevents a conditional classification from silently being
presented as an unconditional proof.

The theorem statements are proved in the separate proof package. Replaying
that package checks their proofs. Deployment still requires faithful input
extraction, authentic runner receipts, correct execution, and a publisher that
respects rejection and publishes the very artifact identified by the approved
run.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Production

open Declarations ProofNetworks Certificates Validation RelativeSoundness Pipeline

/-- A classification retains the assumptions on which it depends. -/
structure Classification where
  assumed : List Nat
  established : List Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Proposed production entry point for classification relative to assumptions. -/
def validateAndClassify (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (initial : List Nat) (certificate : List Step) : Option Classification :=
  match approvedInput key events with
  | none => none
  | some data =>
      let n := network data
      if includes n.statements initial then
        (check n initial certificate).map (fun known =>
          { assumed := initial.eraseDups, established := known })
      else none

/-- Proposed entry point for unconditional proved labels. -/
def validateAndProve (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (certificate : List Step) : Option Classification :=
  validateAndClassify key events [] certificate

/-- The final result is exact for the very snapshot approved by the controller. -/
axiom classification_exact (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (initial : List Nat) (certificate : List Step) (result : Classification)
    (accepted : validateAndClassify key events initial certificate = some result) :
    result.assumed = initial.eraseDups ∧
    ∃ data, approvedInput key events = some data ∧ Valid data ∧
      ∀ a, a ∈ result.established ↔ Derivable (network data) initial a

/-- Main proposed production guarantee. The runner/kernel contract applies to
the actual approved input, not to an unrelated model or an arbitrary network. -/
axiom production_sound (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (certificate : List Step) (result : Classification) (meaning : Nat → Prop)
    (trusted : ∀ data, approvedInput key events = some data → KernelContract data meaning)
    (accepted : validateAndProve key events certificate = some result) :
    result.assumed = [] ∧ ∀ a ∈ result.established, meaning a

/-- A failure in the runner cannot yield a successful final classification. -/
axiom production_rejects_failure (key : ArtifactKey) (events : List Event)
    (failed : Event.failed ∈ events) (initial : List Nat) (certificate : List Step) :
    validateAndClassify key events initial certificate = none

end Lax796640.Production

statements.signature:
classification_exact : ∀ (key : Lax796640.Pipeline.ArtifactKey) (events : List Lax796640.Pipeline.Event) (initial : List Nat)
  (certificate : List Lax796640.Certificates.Step) (result : Lax796640.Production.Classification),
  Eq (Lax796640.Production.validateAndClassify key events initial certificate) (Option.some result) →
    And (Eq result.assumed initial.eraseDups)
      (Exists fun data =>
        And (Eq (Lax796640.Pipeline.approvedInput key events) (Option.some data))
          (And (Lax796640.Validation.Valid data)
            (∀ (a : Nat),
              Iff (List.instMembership.mem result.established a)
                (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable (Lax796640.Validation.network data) initial a))))
statements.doc: The final result is exact for the very snapshot approved by the controller.

statements.signature:
production_rejects_failure : ∀ (key : Lax796640.Pipeline.ArtifactKey) (events : List Lax796640.Pipeline.Event),
  List.instMembership.mem events Lax796640.Pipeline.Event.failed →
    ∀ (initial : List Nat) (certificate : List Lax796640.Certificates.Step),
      Eq (Lax796640.Production.validateAndClassify key events initial certificate) Option.none

statements.signature:
production_sound : ∀ (key : Lax796640.Pipeline.ArtifactKey) (events : List Lax796640.Pipeline.Event)
  (certificate : List Lax796640.Certificates.Step) (result : Lax796640.Production.Classification)
  (meaning : Nat → Prop),
  (∀ (data : Lax796640.Declarations.Snapshot),
      Eq (Lax796640.Pipeline.approvedInput key events) (Option.some data) →
        Lax796640.RelativeSoundness.KernelContract data meaning) →
    Eq (Lax796640.Production.validateAndProve key events certificate) (Option.some result) →
      And (Eq result.assumed List.nil) (∀ (a : Nat), List.instMembership.mem result.established a → meaning a)

the actual approved input, not to an unrelated model or an arbitrary network.

concepts.title: Finite derivations in a proof network
concepts.description:
A proof rule says that its conclusion follows if all its assumptions have
been established. Several rules may have the same conclusion. A derivation
is a finite tree of rule applications, with designated assumptions at its
leaves. A rule with no assumptions supplies a starting point.

The closure algorithm repeatedly applies all available rules. Its result is
specified by finite derivability, independently of the algorithm. The target
equivalence concerns the rules in this snapshot, not all possible Lean proofs.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.Declarations

/-!
---
title: Finite derivations in a proof network
type: theorem
---
A proof rule says that its conclusion follows if all its assumptions have
been established. Several rules may have the same conclusion. A derivation
is a finite tree of rule applications, with designated assumptions at its
leaves. A rule with no assumptions supplies a starting point.

The closure algorithm repeatedly applies all available rules. Its result is
specified by finite derivability, independently of the algorithm. The target
equivalence concerns the rules in this snapshot, not all possible Lean proofs.
-/

namespace Lax796640.ProofNetworks

open Declarations

/-- One conditional proof, identified by its theorem declaration. -/
structure Rule where
  proofId : Nat
  assumptions : List Nat
  conclusion : Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Statements and the available rules for establishing them. -/
structure Network where
  statements : List Nat
  rules : List Rule
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, Repr

/-- Rules refer to existing statements and have distinct proof identifiers. -/
def WellFormed (n : Network) : Prop :=
  n.statements.Nodup ∧ (n.rules.map Rule.proofId).Nodup ∧
  ∀ r ∈ n.rules, r.conclusion ∈ n.statements ∧
    ∀ a ∈ r.assumptions, a ∈ n.statements

/-- Establish a statement from designated assumptions using finitely many rules. -/
inductive Derivable (n : Network) (initial : List Nat) : Nat → Prop where
  | assumption {statement : Nat} :
      statement ∈ initial → Derivable n initial statement
  | apply {r : Rule} : r ∈ n.rules →
      (∀ a ∈ r.assumptions, Derivable n initial a) →
      Derivable n initial r.conclusion

/-- A set is closed when every rule whose assumptions it contains stays in it. -/
def Closed (n : Network) (known : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ n.rules, (∀ a ∈ r.assumptions, a ∈ known) → r.conclusion ∈ known

/-- One round of the executable closure algorithm. -/
def advance (n : Network) (known : List Nat) : List Nat :=
  (known ++ (n.rules.filter (fun r => includes known r.assumptions)).map
    Rule.conclusion).eraseDups

/-- Each recursive call consumes one round. -/
def closeFor (n : Network) : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | 0, known => known.eraseDups
  | rounds + 1, known => closeFor n rounds (advance n known)

/-- At most one round per statement suffices, even in a cyclic network. -/
def closure (n : Network) (initial : List Nat) : List Nat :=
  closeFor n n.statements.length initial

/-- The computed set is exactly the set of finite derivations. -/
axiom closure_exact (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) (statement : Nat) :
    statement ∈ closure n initial ↔ Derivable n initial statement

/-- The bound built into the algorithm reaches a fixed point. -/
axiom closure_closed (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) :
    Closed n (closure n initial)

/-- Without initial assumptions or a rule with no assumptions, nothing starts. -/
axiom no_ungrounded_proof (n : Network)
    (noStart : ∀ r ∈ n.rules, r.assumptions ≠ []) (statement : Nat) :
    ¬ Derivable n [] statement

end Lax796640.ProofNetworks

  Lax796640.ProofNetworks.WellFormed n →
    ∀ (initial : List Nat),
      (∀ (a : Nat), List.instMembership.mem initial a → List.instMembership.mem n.statements a) →
        Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Closed n (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.closure n initial)

concepts.title: What acceptance guarantees under the kernel contract
concepts.description:
Give each declaration identifier the proposition expressed by its type.
The kernel contract below specifies the facts supplied by the trusted Lean
boundary: a checked theorem follows from its actual axiom dependencies,
successful type comparisons preserve meaning, and the permitted background
axioms hold in the chosen interpretation.

These are explicit hypotheses. This submission does not prove Lean's kernel
sound, or establish that an arbitrary JSON report came from that kernel.
Faithful extraction of declaration references and comparisons is necessary
to apply the contract to the real archive.

The important intermediate claim is derived rather than assumed: validation
turns these declaration-level facts into sound proof-network rules. Finite
derivations then compose those rules. A valid conditional proof may still
have unproved assumptions; acceptance alone does not discharge them.

import Lax796640.Validation
import Lax796640.Certificates

/-!
---
title: What acceptance guarantees under the kernel contract
type: theorem
---
Give each declaration identifier the proposition expressed by its type.
The kernel contract below specifies the facts supplied by the trusted Lean
boundary: a checked theorem follows from its actual axiom dependencies,
successful type comparisons preserve meaning, and the permitted background
axioms hold in the chosen interpretation.

These are explicit hypotheses. This submission does not prove Lean's kernel
sound, or establish that an arbitrary JSON report came from that kernel.
Faithful extraction of declaration references and comparisons is necessary
to apply the contract to the real archive.

The important intermediate claim is derived rather than assumed: validation
turns these declaration-level facts into sound proof-network rules. Finite
derivations then compose those rules. A valid conditional proof may still
have unproved assumptions; acceptance alone does not discharge them.
-/

namespace Lax796640.RelativeSoundness

open Declarations Dependencies ProofNetworks Validation Certificates

/-- The explicit logical interface to replay and faithful inspection.
`meaning id` denotes the proposition expressed by the declaration's type;
the contract is used only for theorems and their axiom dependencies.
-/
structure KernelContract (s : Snapshot) (meaning : Nat → Prop) : Prop where
  /-- Kernel-checked theorem bodies establish their types from their axiom leaves. -/
  theoremSound : ∀ d ∈ s.declarations, d.kind = .theoremDecl →
    (∀ a, UsesAxiom s d.id a → meaning a) → meaning d.id
  /-- Conversion compares the actual types, rather than their printed text. -/
  comparisonSound : ∀ f ∈ s.comparisons, f.sameType = true →
    (meaning f.theoremId ↔ meaning f.statementId)
  /-- The three permitted background axioms hold in the chosen interpretation. -/
  backgroundSound : ∀ a, backgroundAxiom s a = true → meaning a

/-- Each recorded rule preserves truth when all of its assumptions hold. -/
def RulesSound (n : Network) (meaning : Nat → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ n.rules, (∀ a ∈ r.assumptions, meaning a) → meaning r.conclusion

/-- The validator's acceptance rules justify the edges it records. -/
axiom validation_rules_sound (s : Snapshot) (meaning : Nat → Prop)
    (kernel : KernelContract s meaning) (accepted : validate s = true) :
    RulesSound (network s) meaning

/-- Finite derivations compose sound rules without introducing new assumptions. -/
axiom derivation_sound (n : Network) (meaning : Nat → Prop)
    (rules : RulesSound n meaning) (initial : List Nat)
    (assumptions : ∀ a ∈ initial, meaning a) (a : Nat)
    (derived : Derivable n initial a) : meaning a

/-- Main mathematical guarantee for the computed closure of accepted records. -/
axiom established_sound (s : Snapshot) (meaning : Nat → Prop)
    (kernel : KernelContract s meaning) (accepted : validate s = true)
    (initial : List Nat) (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ (network s).statements)
    (assumptions : ∀ a ∈ initial, meaning a) (a : Nat)
    (established : a ∈ closure (network s) initial) : meaning a

/-- The same guarantee holds when an arbitrary producer supplies a certificate. -/
axiom certificate_sound (s : Snapshot) (meaning : Nat → Prop)
    (kernel : KernelContract s meaning) (accepted : validate s = true)
    (initial : List Nat) (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ (network s).statements)
    (assumptions : ∀ a ∈ initial, meaning a) (steps : List Step)
    (known : List Nat) (certificate : check (network s) initial steps = some known)
    (a : Nat) (established : a ∈ known) : meaning a

end Lax796640.RelativeSoundness

  Lax796640.RelativeSoundness.KernelContract s meaning →

      ∀ (initial : List Nat),
        (∀ (a : Nat),
            List.instMembership.mem initial a → List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.Validation.network s).statements a) →
          (∀ (a : Nat), List.instMembership.mem initial a → meaning a) →

concepts.title: Adding proofs, discharging assumptions, and renaming statements
concepts.description:
Several archive operations should preserve existing derivations. Adding
available proofs cannot invalidate one. Assumptions can be replaced by their
own derivations. Reordering the available rules does not change what follows.
Renaming identifiers consistently also preserves the result, provided the
renaming does not merge distinct statements.

These statements concern immutable mathematical networks. Replacing an
archived submission is covered only when the replacement satisfies the
stated network relationship; a successor label alone is not such a proof.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.ProofNetworks

/-!
---
title: Adding proofs, discharging assumptions, and renaming statements
type: theorem
---
Several archive operations should preserve existing derivations. Adding
available proofs cannot invalidate one. Assumptions can be replaced by their
own derivations. Reordering the available rules does not change what follows.
Renaming identifiers consistently also preserves the result, provided the
renaming does not merge distinct statements.

These statements concern immutable mathematical networks. Replacing an
archived submission is covered only when the replacement satisfies the
stated network relationship; a successor label alone is not such a proof.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Stability

open ProofNetworks

/-- Every original rule remains available in an extension. -/
def Extends (original extended : Network) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ original.rules, r ∈ extended.rules

/-- Rename statement identifiers in assumptions and conclusions. Proof ids stay fixed. -/
def rename (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Network) : Network where
  statements := n.statements.map f
  rules := n.rules.map (fun r =>
    { r with assumptions := r.assumptions.map f, conclusion := f r.conclusion })

/-- Adding rules preserves all existing finite derivations. -/
axiom extension_preserves (n larger : Network) (extension : Extends n larger)
    (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat) :
    Derivable n initial a → Derivable larger initial a

/-- Derivations of the assumptions can be substituted into a derivation. -/
axiom discharge_assumptions (n : Network) (initial replacement : List Nat)
    (discharge : ∀ a ∈ initial, Derivable n replacement a) (a : Nat) :
    Derivable n initial a → Derivable n replacement a

/-- The order and multiplicity of identical proof rules have no semantic effect. -/
axiom rules_order_irrelevant (left right : Network)
    (sameRules : ∀ r, r ∈ left.rules ↔ r ∈ right.rules)
    (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat) :
    Derivable left initial a ↔ Derivable right initial a

/-- An injective renaming preserves and reflects derivability. -/
axiom renaming_exact (n : Network) (f : Nat → Nat) (injective : Function.Injective f)
    (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat) :
    Derivable (rename f n) (initial.map f) (f a) ↔ Derivable n initial a

/-- Recomputing closure from an already closed result changes no membership. -/
axiom closure_idempotent (n : Network) (h : WellFormed n) (initial : List Nat)
    (admitted : ∀ a ∈ initial, a ∈ n.statements) (a : Nat) :
    a ∈ closure n (closure n initial) ↔ a ∈ closure n initial

end Lax796640.Stability

  Lax796640.ProofNetworks.WellFormed n →
    ∀ (initial : List Nat),

        ∀ (a : Nat),
          Iff
            (List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.closure n (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.closure n initial)) a)
            (List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.closure n initial) a)

  (∀ (a : Nat), List.instMembership.mem initial a → Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable n replacement a) →
    ∀ (a : Nat), Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable n initial a → Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable n replacement a
statements.doc: Derivations of the assumptions can be substituted into a derivation.

    ∀ (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat),
      Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable n initial a → Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable larger initial a

    ∀ (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat),
      Iff (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable (Lax796640.Stability.rename f n) (List.map f initial) (f a))
        (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable n initial a)

      Iff (List.instMembership.mem left.rules r) (List.instMembership.mem right.rules r)) →
    ∀ (initial : List Nat) (a : Nat),
      Iff (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable left initial a) (Lax796640.ProofNetworks.Derivable right initial a)

concepts.title: The executable mathematical validation rules
concepts.description:
Validation has two descriptions here. `Valid` states the requirements using
quantifiers and graph reachability. `validate` is a concrete Boolean program
using finite lists and the executable axiom collector. The central obligation
is that these descriptions agree on every input.

Only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound` are permitted background
axioms. A concept may state an axiom but may not use another statement as an
assumption. Proof declarations may use background axioms and statements from
directly required concept packages. A proof claim must name a theorem with
the same type as its imported conclusion.

These are mathematical acceptance rules. Source fetching, declaration
extraction, namespaces, documentation, paper rendering, and ownership checks
are outside this function. Package roles and kernel comparisons must be
authenticated by the surrounding pipeline; their presence in this data
structure is not authentication.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax796640.Dependencies
import Lax796640.ProofNetworks

/-!
---
title: The executable mathematical validation rules
type: theorem
---
Validation has two descriptions here. `Valid` states the requirements using
quantifiers and graph reachability. `validate` is a concrete Boolean program
using finite lists and the executable axiom collector. The central obligation
is that these descriptions agree on every input.

Only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound` are permitted background
axioms. A concept may state an axiom but may not use another statement as an
assumption. Proof declarations may use background axioms and statements from
directly required concept packages. A proof claim must name a theorem with
the same type as its imported conclusion.

These are mathematical acceptance rules. Source fetching, declaration
extraction, namespaces, documentation, paper rendering, and ownership checks
are outside this function. Package roles and kernel comparisons must be
authenticated by the surrounding pipeline; their presence in this data
structure is not authentication.
-/

namespace Lax796640.Validation

open Declarations Dependencies ProofNetworks

/-- The fixed background axiom policy of the intended Lax environment. -/
def backgroundNames : List String :=
  ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]

/-- A background axiom must have both the right name and a background origin. -/
def backgroundAxiom (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : Bool :=
  (declaration s id).any (fun d =>
    d.kind == .axiomDecl && backgroundNames.contains d.name &&
    (package s d.package).any (fun p => p.role == .background))

/-- An admissible statement is a propositional axiom of a concept package. -/
def isStatement (s : Snapshot) (id : Nat) : Bool :=
  (declaration s id).any (fun d =>
    d.kind == .axiomDecl && d.isProposition &&
    (package s d.package).any (fun p => p.role == .concepts))

/-- A proof package may assume statements only from directly required concepts. -/
def allowedStatement (s : Snapshot) (proofPackage statement : Nat) : Bool :=
  isStatement s statement &&
    (package s proofPackage).any (fun p =>
      (declaration s statement).any (fun d => p.requires.contains d.package))

/-- An explicit successful comparison for this particular theorem and conclusion. -/
def comparisonAgrees (s : Snapshot) (c : Claim) : Bool :=
  s.comparisons.any (fun f => f.theoremId == c.theoremId &&
    f.statementId == c.statementId && f.sameType && f.conclusionImported)

/-- Statements used by a theorem, after removing permitted background axioms. -/
def assumptionsOf (s : Snapshot) (theoremId : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (axiomsUsed s theoremId).filter (fun a => !(backgroundAxiom s a))

/-- Declarative requirements on identifiers, package relationships, and references. -/
def TablesValid (s : Snapshot) : Prop :=
  ReferencesWellFormed s ∧
  (s.declarations.map Declaration.name).Nodup ∧
  (s.packages.map Package.id).Nodup ∧ s.localPackages.Nodup ∧
  (∀ id ∈ s.localPackages, ∃ p ∈ s.packages, p.id = id) ∧
  (∀ d ∈ s.declarations, ∃ p ∈ s.packages, p.id = d.package) ∧
  (∀ p ∈ s.packages,
    p.environment = s.environment ∧
    (p.role = .background ∨ p.id ∈ s.localPackages ∨ p.registered = true) ∧
    (∀ id ∈ p.requires, ∃ q ∈ s.packages, q.id = id) ∧
    (p.role = .concepts → ∀ id ∈ p.requires,
      ∀ q ∈ s.packages, q.id = id → q.role ≠ .proofs)) ∧
  (∀ f ∈ s.comparisons,
    (∃ d ∈ s.declarations, d.id = f.theoremId) ∧
    (∃ d ∈ s.declarations, d.id = f.statementId))

/-- The axiom policy for one declaration, stated without the collector program. -/
def DeclarationValid (s : Snapshot) (d : Declaration) : Prop :=
  ∃ p ∈ s.packages, p.id = d.package ∧
    match p.role with
    | .background => True
    | .concepts =>
        (d.kind = .axiomDecl → d.isProposition = true) ∧
        ∀ a, UsesAxiom s d.id a →
          backgroundAxiom s a = true ∨ (d.kind = .axiomDecl ∧ a = d.id)
    | .proofs =>
        ∀ a, UsesAxiom s d.id a →
          backgroundAxiom s a = true ∨ allowedStatement s d.package a = true

/-- A proof claim agrees with declaration facts and with its actual dependencies. -/
def ClaimValid (s : Snapshot) (c : Claim) : Prop :=
  ∃ d ∈ s.declarations, d.id = c.theoremId ∧ d.kind = .theoremDecl ∧
    (package s d.package).any (fun p => p.role == .proofs) = true ∧
    allowedStatement s d.package c.statementId = true ∧
    comparisonAgrees s c = true ∧
    ∀ claimed, c.claimedAssumptions = some claimed →
      ∀ a, a ∈ claimed ↔ UsesAxiom s c.theoremId a ∧ backgroundAxiom s a = false

/-- The independent mathematical specification of acceptance. -/
def Valid (s : Snapshot) : Prop :=
  TablesValid s ∧ (∀ d ∈ s.declarations, DeclarationValid s d) ∧
  (s.claims.map Claim.theoremId).Nodup ∧ (∀ c ∈ s.claims, ClaimValid s c)

/-- Check finite table integrity before relying on lookups. -/
def checkTables (s : Snapshot) : Bool :=
  let declIds := s.declarations.map Declaration.id
  let declNames := s.declarations.map Declaration.name
  let packageIds := s.packages.map Package.id
  declIds.eraseDups.length == declIds.length &&
  declNames.eraseDups.length == declNames.length &&
  packageIds.eraseDups.length == packageIds.length &&
  s.localPackages.eraseDups.length == s.localPackages.length &&
  includes packageIds s.localPackages &&
  s.declarations.all (fun d => packageIds.contains d.package &&
    includes declIds d.references) &&
  s.packages.all (fun p => p.environment == s.environment &&
    (p.role == .background || s.localPackages.contains p.id || p.registered) &&
    includes packageIds p.requires &&
    (p.role != .concepts || p.requires.all (fun id =>
      (package s id).any (fun q => q.role != .proofs)))) &&
  s.comparisons.all (fun f => declIds.contains f.theoremId &&
    declIds.contains f.statementId)

/-- Check the declaration policy using computed axiom dependencies. -/
def checkDeclaration (s : Snapshot) (d : Declaration) : Bool :=
  match package s d.package with
  | none => false
  | some p =>
      match p.role with
      | .background => true
      | .concepts =>
          (d.kind != .axiomDecl || d.isProposition) &&
          (axiomsUsed s d.id).all (fun a => backgroundAxiom s a ||
            (d.kind == .axiomDecl && a == d.id))
      | .proofs =>
          (axiomsUsed s d.id).all (fun a => backgroundAxiom s a ||
            allowedStatement s d.package a)

/-- Check a proof claim; author-supplied assumptions can never hide a dependency. -/
def checkClaim (s : Snapshot) (c : Claim) : Bool :=
  (declaration s c.theoremId).any (fun d =>
    d.kind == .theoremDecl &&
    (package s d.package).any (fun p => p.role == .proofs) &&
    allowedStatement s d.package c.statementId && comparisonAgrees s c &&
    match c.claimedAssumptions with
    | none => true
    | some claimed => sameMembers claimed (assumptionsOf s c.theoremId))

/-- Proposed production entry point for mathematical validation.
This function is executable; it does not call any stated proof obligation. -/
def validate (s : Snapshot) : Bool :=
  checkTables s && s.declarations.all (checkDeclaration s) &&
  (s.claims.map Claim.theoremId).eraseDups.length == s.claims.length &&
  s.claims.all (checkClaim s)

/-- The network recorded after acceptance, built from recomputed assumptions. -/
def network (s : Snapshot) : Network where
  statements := (s.declarations.map Declaration.id).filter (isStatement s)
  rules := s.claims.map (fun c =>
    { proofId := c.theoremId, assumptions := assumptionsOf s c.theoremId,
      conclusion := c.statementId })

/-- No network is returned when the mathematical rules fail. -/
def acceptedNetwork (s : Snapshot) : Option Network :=
  if validate s then some (network s) else none

/-- Exact agreement between the executable validator and its specification. -/
axiom validate_exact (s : Snapshot) : validate s = true ↔ Valid s

/-- Accepted records produce a network with no dangling or duplicate identities. -/
axiom accepted_network_wellFormed (s : Snapshot) (accepted : validate s = true) :
    WellFormed (network s)

/-- Every recorded assumption is an actual, non-background axiom dependency. -/
axiom recorded_assumptions_exact (s : Snapshot) (accepted : validate s = true)
    (c : Claim) (present : c ∈ s.claims) (a : Nat) :
    a ∈ assumptionsOf s c.theoremId ↔
      UsesAxiom s c.theoremId a ∧ backgroundAxiom s a = false

end Lax796640.Validation

  Eq (Lax796640.Validation.validate s) Bool.true →
    ∀ (c : Lax796640.Declarations.Claim),
      List.instMembership.mem s.claims c →
        ∀ (a : Nat),
          Iff (List.instMembership.mem (Lax796640.Validation.assumptionsOf s c.theoremId) a)
            (And (Lax796640.Dependencies.UsesAxiom s c.theoremId a)
              (Eq (Lax796640.Validation.backgroundAxiom s a) Bool.false))
statements.doc: Every recorded assumption is an actual, non-background axiom dependency.

statements.signature:
validate_exact : ∀ (s : Lax796640.Declarations.Snapshot),
  Iff (Eq (Lax796640.Validation.validate s) Bool.true) (Lax796640.Validation.Valid s)
statements.doc: Exact agreement between the executable validator and its specification.

proofs.description:
Keep adding an enabled conclusion that is still missing. Each step consumes a
distinct statement, so the process reaches closure within the stated bound.

Ordered witnesses justify every added statement. The final closure check then
contains every finite derivation, so no derivable statement is omitted.

Exactness turns an omitted statement into a certificate of non-derivability
from the available rules, without asserting that the statement is false.

Filtering the exact reachability result by declaration kind gives exactly the
used axioms, including an axiom's dependency on itself.

The finite bound saturates the reference graph. Every added reference extends
a path, and every finite path lies in the saturated set.

The controller invariant links every accepted receipt to this artifact and
this run. Approval additionally supplies the environment and validation checks.
Failure is recorded permanently; later successful receipts cannot clear it.
A fresh controller state has none of the receipts required for approval.

Successful execution identifies the very inspected snapshot that passed the
controller and validator. The certificate result is exact for that network,
and the returned assumptions are precisely the supplied assumptions.

The final entry point immediately rejects whenever the controller records a
failure, regardless of the proposed assumptions or certificate.

The unconditional entry point supplies no assumptions. Exact classification
therefore gives a finite derivation from sound rules for every proved label,
under the kernel contract for the actual approved snapshot.

If another round could add a statement, the strictly growing finite set would
already have exceeded the number of statements in the network.

Each round only adds valid rule conclusions. Conversely, the fixed point
contains the leaves and is closed under every rule in a finite derivation.

A finite derivation must have a leaf. With no assumptions and no rule without
premises, even a cycle cannot supply one.

The certificate checker supplies the same finite derivations without trusting
the program that produced the certificate.
Induction on a finite derivation composes truth-preserving rules.

The concrete closure algorithm produces finite derivations, whose rules are
sound under the explicit kernel contract.

Partition a theorem's actual axiom dependencies into background axioms and
recorded assumptions. The kernel contract establishes the theorem, and its
successful type comparison transfers that meaning to the claimed conclusion.

An assumption in the first closure already has a derivation from the original
assumptions. Substituting those derivations makes a second closure redundant.
Replace each assumption leaf with its supplied derivation.
Reuse the same finite derivation in the larger network.

Map the derivation in one direction. Injectivity permits each mapped rule and
assumption to be recovered in the other direction.
Rule membership is the only feature of the rule list used by derivations.

Validation supplies unique statement and proof identifiers. Every conclusion
and recomputed assumption is an admitted concept statement in the table.

The stored assumptions come from the actual dependency traversal, with exactly
the permitted background axioms removed.

Unique table identifiers make lookups exact. The dependency collector is exact
as well, so each Boolean check is equivalent to its declarative requirement.
